summary: Both acceptance items hold: the 20 snapshots are byte-identical to 569ee8f and docs/build.py --check passes. The label text agrees with the snapshot values and with the CORE-07 verifier's finding. All 40 snapshot links on the 20 dataset pages carry the label linked to the reference's #signs-and-frames section. checks.area: label accuracy against the YAML values
evidence: Run pelvis_sagittal_angle_rad is identical in all four families: [-0.05,0.67] / [-0.05,0.63] / [-0.05,0.68] / [-0.05,0.63] at 0/25/50/75%, centred about +0.30 rad. Under rule B that is about 17° posterior tilt while running, so it reads anterior-positive (old sign). This agrees with CORE-07-verify round 1 check 2.

Walking and stair (85db family only, checked in ca23): incline centres are +0.07…+0.24, stair_ascent +0.25/+0.19 and decline −0.32…−0.17. Incline and stair ascent sit above level, and level above decline, so they read anterior-positive. This agrees with CORE-07-verify round 2 ('they read anterior-positive, not mixed').

Sit/stand: sit_to_stand centres go from +0.33 seated to −0.22 mid-rise, and stand_to_sit goes negative while lowering. Forward tilt while rising and lowering is negative, so these already read as rule B. The label correctly makes no claim about them. Transition bands are near-symmetric and are not mentioned.

Optional note: the fc02, f21f and 6abe families (9 snapshots) contain pelvis entries only for run, sit/stand and transition, with no walking or stair pelvis entries. On those pages the 'walking and stair' part of the label refers to entries that do not exist. That is harmless (no current-sign entry is mislabelled), but 'run (and, where present, walking and stair) pelvis entries' would be exact.

checks.evidence: I parsed every docs/datasets/*/index.html. 20 pages link a snapshot, each twice (40 links), and each link is followed within its list item or paragraph by <small class="legacy-sign-label">. That makes 40 labels, each with the single href ../../reference/index.html#signs-and-frames and the stated text. The anchor id='signs-and-frames' exists once in docs/reference/index.html. No other HTML, JS or JSON file under docs/ (excluding maintainers and audits) links a *_validation_ranges.yaml.

evidence: _legacy_snapshot_label reads DOCS_DATASETS_DIR/<basename> and returns the label only if its SHA-256 is one of the four legacy hashes. It returns '' for None, a missing file or an OSError.

Scratchpad probe with DOCS_DATASETS_DIR redirected to a scratch folder: a byte copy of the gt21 snapshot gets the label; current default_ranges.yaml (a fresh snapshot) gets ''; a legacy copy with one appended comment line gets ''; a missing name and a traversal name ('../../etc/passwd', reduced to its basename) both get ''. The real gt21 snapshot path gets the label.

Ordering: in the add/update-validation flows, _snapshot_validation_ranges copies the new snapshot (shutil.copyfile) before generate_dataset_page and generate_validation_page compute the label. A regenerated snapshot is therefore hashed after it is written, so a page cannot keep a stale label. update-documentation does not rewrite the snapshot and hashes the existing file.

Residual by design: a re-snapshot of old-sign ranges whose bytes differ (e.g. a new 'generated' timestamp) would get no label, so the gate can miss a label but cannot attach a wrong one. The CORE-07 tests pin the 20 snapshots' bytes, which bounds this.
